title: Jonah Chapter 4 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Jonah chapter 4 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Jonah Chapter 4 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Jonah Chapter 4.

questions.question: How did Jonah feel after the events described in the earlier chapters, according to Jonah 4:1?
options: He was exceedingly displeased and very angry
questions.correctAnswer: He was exceedingly displeased and very angry
questions.explanation: Jonah 4:1 states that it displeased Jonah exceedingly, and he was very angry.

questions.question: Who did Jonah pray to in Jonah 4:2?
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD
questions.explanation: Jonah 4:2 explicitly says Jonah prayed unto the LORD.

questions.question: In Jonah 4:2, Jonah mentions fleeing to which place before?
questions.correctAnswer: Tarshish
questions.explanation: Jonah 4:2 says Jonah fled before unto Tarshish.

questions.question: What attributes of God does Jonah mention in his prayer in Jonah 4:2?
options: Gracious, merciful, slow to anger, great kindness, and repents of evil
questions.correctAnswer: Gracious, merciful, slow to anger, great kindness, and repents of evil
questions.explanation: Jonah 4:2 describes God as gracious, merciful, slow to anger, of great kindness, and repents of evil.

questions.question: What did Jonah request from the LORD in Jonah 4:3?
options: To bless the people of Nineveh
To give him strength to continue
To take his life because it is better to die than to live
To send him to Tarshish again
questions.correctAnswer: To take his life because it is better to die than to live
questions.explanation: Jonah 4:3 states Jonah beseeches the LORD to take his life, saying it is better to die than live.

questions.question: What question did the LORD ask Jonah in Jonah 4:4?
options: Will you forgive the people of Nineveh?
Doest thou well to be angry?
Will you go to Tarshish again?
Do you want me to send another prophet?
questions.correctAnswer: Doest thou well to be angry?
questions.explanation: Jonah 4:4 records the LORD asking Jonah if it is right for him to be angry.

questions.question: True or False: Jonah built a booth on the west side of the city to watch what would happen.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jonah 4:5 says Jonah sat on the east side of the city and made a booth there.

questions.question: True or False: According to Jonah 4:6, God prepared a gourd to give Jonah shade and relieve his grief.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jonah 4:6 states that God prepared a gourd to come up over Jonah to give him shade and relieve his grief.

questions.question: What happened to the gourd the morning after it grew over Jonah, according to Jonah 4:7?
options: It withered because a worm smote it
It was taken away by the wind
questions.correctAnswer: It withered because a worm smote it
questions.explanation: Jonah 4:7 states God prepared a worm that smote the gourd and it withered.

questions.question: What natural elements caused Jonah to faint and wish to die in Jonah 4:8?
options: A violent east wind and the sun beating on his head
questions.correctAnswer: A violent east wind and the sun beating on his head
questions.explanation: Jonah 4:8 describes a vehement east wind and the sun beating on Jonah’s head causing him to faint and wish to die.

questions.question: True or False: Jonah said it was wrong to be angry about the gourd's death.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jonah 4:9 shows Jonah affirmed that he was right to be angry even to death over the gourd.

questions.question: According to Jonah 4:10, how long did the gourd last?
options: It grew and lasted a year
It came up in a night and perished in a night
questions.correctAnswer: It came up in a night and perished in a night
questions.explanation: Jonah 4:10 says the gourd came up in a night and perished in a night.

questions.question: What reason does God give for sparing Nineveh in Jonah 4:11?
options: They were a small town with few people
There were more than sixty thousand persons who cannot discern between their right hand and their left hand, and many cattle
questions.correctAnswer: There were more than sixty thousand persons who cannot discern between their right hand and their left hand, and many cattle
questions.explanation: Jonah 4:11 describes Nineveh as a great city with more than sixscore thousand persons who cannot discern between right and left hand, and much cattle.

questions.question: True or False: Jonah was glad about the gourd because it provided him shade and relief from his grief.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jonah 4:6 states Jonah was exceeding glad of the gourd because it gave him shade and relief.

questions.question: In Jonah 4, which event happened first?
options: God prepared a worm to smite the gourd
Jonah sat in a booth to watch the city
God prepared a gourd to shade Jonah
questions.correctAnswer: Jonah prayed to the LORD
questions.explanation: Jonah first prayed to the LORD in verse 2, then sat in a booth (verse 5), then God prepared the gourd (verse 6), and finally God prepared the worm (verse 7).

medium.title: Jonah Chapter 4 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Jonah Chapter 4 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did Jonah do after he left the city, according to Jonah 4:5?
options: He went to pray in the temple
He sat on the east side of the city and made a booth
He went to find the people of Nineveh
questions.correctAnswer: He sat on the east side of the city and made a booth
questions.explanation: Jonah 4:5 states that Jonah went out of the city, sat on the east side, made a booth, and sat under it to see what would happen to the city. This shows Jonah's watchful and expectant attitude after preaching.

questions.question: How does Jonah 4:6 demonstrate God's compassion towards Jonah?
options: God sent rain to cool Jonah
God prepared a gourd to give Jonah shade and relieve his grief
God sent angels to comfort Jonah
God gave Jonah a new mission
questions.correctAnswer: God prepared a gourd to give Jonah shade and relieve his grief
questions.explanation: Jonah 4:6 shows God’s care by preparing a gourd to provide shade over Jonah’s head, delivering him from his grief. This reveals God's kindness even when Jonah is angry or distressed.

questions.question: What was the purpose of the gourd that God prepared for Jonah?
options: To teach a lesson about plants
questions.correctAnswer: To provide shade and comfort
questions.explanation: Jonah 4:6 explains that the gourd came up over Jonah to give him a shadow over his head, relieving his grief and making him exceedingly glad. It illustrates God's practical mercy.

questions.question: According to Jonah 4:7, what caused the gourd to wither?
questions.correctAnswer: A worm prepared by God
questions.explanation: Jonah 4:7 states that God prepared a worm at dawn to smite the gourd, causing it to wither. This shows God's control over nature to teach Jonah a lesson.

questions.question: What happened to Jonah when the sun rose, as described in Jonah 4:8?
options: He rejoiced in the morning light
He fainted from the heat and wished to die
questions.correctAnswer: He fainted from the heat and wished to die
questions.explanation: Jonah 4:8 recounts that a vehement east wind and the sun beating on Jonah caused him to faint and wish he were dead, showing his emotional and physical distress.

questions.question: How does Jonah 4:9 show Jonah's attitude toward the loss of the gourd?
options: He was angry even to death
He thanked God for the lesson
questions.correctAnswer: He was angry even to death
questions.explanation: Jonah 4:9 reveals Jonah’s intense anger over the gourd’s loss, stating he was angry unto death, which contrasts with God's mercy toward Nineveh.

questions.question: What lesson does God emphasize in Jonah 4:10 about Jonah's concern for the gourd?
options: Jonah had lovingly cared for the gourd
Jonah had no part in the gourd's growth, which came up and perished quickly
The gourd was a symbol of Jonah's pride
questions.correctAnswer: Jonah had no part in the gourd's growth, which came up and perished quickly
questions.explanation: Jonah 4:10 teaches that Jonah had not labored for or made the gourd grow, which appeared and disappeared overnight, highlighting the temporary nature of his concern.

questions.question: Based on Jonah 4:11, why does God argue He should spare Nineveh?
options: Because Nineveh is a small village
Because there are many innocent people and animals there
questions.correctAnswer: Because there are many innocent people and animals there
questions.explanation: Jonah 4:11 emphasizes that Nineveh has more than 120,000 people who cannot discern right from left, plus many cattle, suggesting God’s mercy extends to innocent lives deserving compassion.

questions.question: How does Jonah 4:5-6 illustrate the biblical virtue of patience in the face of disappointment?
options: Jonah immediately leaves the city without concern
Jonah waits in a booth to see what happens, and God provides a gourd to ease his grief
Jonah prays for the city’s destruction
questions.correctAnswer: Jonah waits in a booth to see what happens, and God provides a gourd to ease his grief
questions.explanation: Verses 5 and 6 show Jonah patiently watching Nineveh's fate, and God’s provision of the gourd teaches us about divine compassion and the importance of endurance during trials.

questions.question: What does Jonah 4:7-8 teach about God’s control over circumstances that affect human emotions?
options: God is unaware of earthly events
God directly orchestrated the worm and the east wind to influence Jonah's feelings
Jonah’s feelings are independent of God’s will
questions.correctAnswer: God directly orchestrated the worm and the east wind to influence Jonah's feelings
questions.explanation: Jonah 4:7-8 describes God preparing the worm and the east wind causing Jonah’s suffering, illustrating God’s sovereignty over nature and human experience to teach important lessons.

questions.question: A believer struggles with anger when things do not go as planned. Based on Jonah 4:4 and 4:9, what biblical truth can help them?
options: It is right to be angry without reflection
God questions whether anger is justified and encourages self-examination
Anger should be ignored and suppressed
Anger is a sign of spiritual failure
questions.correctAnswer: God questions whether anger is justified and encourages self-examination
questions.explanation: Jonah 4:4 and 4:9 show God asking Jonah if his anger is right, prompting reflection on emotions and encouraging humility and understanding rather than unchecked anger.

questions.question: What practical Christian living lesson can we learn from Jonah 4:6-8 about how God uses circumstances to teach us?
options: God uses both comfort and hardship to instruct and grow our faith
Trials should be avoided at all costs
questions.correctAnswer: God uses both comfort and hardship to instruct and grow our faith
questions.explanation: Jonah 4:6-8 shows God giving Jonah comfort through the gourd and hardship through the worm and wind, teaching that God’s ways include both to develop character and dependence on Him.

questions.question: True or False: Jonah was glad when the gourd was destroyed because it reminded him of God's sovereignty.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jonah 4:6-9 shows Jonah was exceeding glad of the gourd but became angry to death when it withered, indicating he was not glad at its destruction but upset.

questions.question: True or False: Jonah’s desire to die rather than live, as seen in Jonah 4:3 and 4:8, reflects his deep emotional struggle and frustration with God's mercy toward Nineveh.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jonah 4:3 and 4:8 reveal Jonah’s repeated wish to die, showing his profound distress and inability to accept God's compassion toward the city, highlighting human struggle with divine mercy.

questions.question: True or False: Jonah 4:11 teaches that God's mercy is limited only to those who fully understand right from wrong.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jonah 4:11 states that God should spare Nineveh despite many who cannot discern their right hand from their left, showing God's mercy extends even to those who lack full understanding.

hard.title: Jonah Chapter 4 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Jonah Chapter 4.

questions.question: What reason does God give Jonah for sparing the city of Nineveh?
options: Because it was the capital city
Because many people and animals lived there who could not discern between right and left
Because it was a small town
questions.correctAnswer: Because many people and animals lived there who could not discern between right and left
questions.explanation: Jonah 4:11 states that God spares Nineveh because it is a great city with more than sixty thousand persons who cannot discern between their right hand and their left hand, and also many cattle.

questions.question: How does Jonah respond when God asks if he is right to be angry about the gourd?
options: He says he is not angry at all
He says he is angry only a little
He says he is angry even unto death
questions.correctAnswer: He says he is angry even unto death
questions.explanation: Jonah 4:9 records Jonah's response to God's question, where Jonah admits he is angry even unto death.

questions.question: What literary device is primarily used in the contrast between the gourd's growth and its sudden destruction in Jonah 4?
questions.correctAnswer: Chiasm
questions.explanation: The rapid rise and sudden destruction of the gourd in Jonah 4:10 form a chiasm that emphasizes the temporary nature of Jonah's comfort compared to God's enduring mercy on Nineveh.

questions.question: What Hebrew meaning of the word 'repentest' in Jonah 4:2 helps explain God's character?
questions.correctAnswer: To regret or change mind
questions.explanation: In Jonah 4:2, 'repentest' comes from the Hebrew root 'nacham,' meaning to regret or change one’s mind, highlighting God's merciful and gracious nature.

questions.question: What does Jonah do after God questions his anger in Jonah 4:4?
options: He goes out of the city and makes a booth to sit under
questions.correctAnswer: He goes out of the city and makes a booth to sit under
questions.explanation: Jonah 4:5 states that after God's question, Jonah leaves the city, makes a booth on the east side, and sits under it to watch what happens to the city.

questions.question: How does God provide relief to Jonah from his grief in Jonah 4?
options: By creating a gourd to give shade
By sending a servant to comfort him
questions.correctAnswer: By creating a gourd to give shade
questions.explanation: Jonah 4:6 says God prepared a gourd to grow over Jonah, providing shade and relieving his grief.

questions.question: What happens to the gourd that shaded Jonah?
options: It withers after a worm smites it
It is cut down by men
questions.correctAnswer: It withers after a worm smites it
questions.explanation: Jonah 4:7 describes how God prepared a worm that smote the gourd, causing it to wither.

questions.question: What natural elements cause Jonah to faint and wish to die after the gourd withers?
options: A vehement east wind and the sun beating on his head
questions.correctAnswer: A vehement east wind and the sun beating on his head
questions.explanation: Jonah 4:8 states that God prepared a vehement east wind and the sun beat upon Jonah’s head, causing him to faint and wish to die.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of God's mercy towards the repentant, as shown in Jonah 4:11?
questions.correctAnswer: Luke 15:11-32 (The Prodigal Son)
questions.explanation: Luke 15:11-32 echoes God's mercy and forgiveness toward sinners who repent, paralleling the theme of Jonah 4:11 where God spares repentant Nineveh.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage shares the theme of God’s compassion and willingness to relent from sending calamity, similar to Jonah 4:2?
questions.correctAnswer: Exodus 34:6-7
questions.explanation: Exodus 34:6-7 describes God as merciful, gracious, slow to anger, and abounding in steadfast love, directly paralleling Jonah 4:2’s description of God's character.

questions.question: What does Jonah request from God in his prayer in Jonah 4:3?
options: To take his life because he prefers death to life
To send a prophet to Nineveh
questions.correctAnswer: To take his life because he prefers death to life
questions.explanation: Jonah 4:3 shows Jonah praying to God asking to take his life, stating it is better for him to die than live.

questions.question: What is the significance of Jonah sitting on the east side of the city in Jonah 4:5?
options: It symbolizes facing the rising sun and awaiting God’s judgment
It is where the city gates were located
It was the coldest side of the city
It was the side closest to Tarshish
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes facing the rising sun and awaiting God’s judgment
questions.explanation: Sitting on the east side (Jonah 4:5) can symbolically represent Jonah watching the sunrise and the unfolding of God’s judgment or mercy on the city.

questions.question: True or False: Jonah created the gourd plant to shade himself and relieve his grief.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jonah 4:10 explains that Jonah had no role in creating or growing the gourd; God prepared it to give Jonah shade.

questions.question: True or False: Jonah's anger in this chapter exemplifies human struggle to accept God's mercy on undeserving people.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jonah 4:1, 9-11 show Jonah's anger at God's mercy towards Nineveh, illustrating the human difficulty in accepting divine compassion for others.

questions.question: Which theme from Jonah 4 is fulfilled in Jesus’ parable about the lost sheep in Luke 15:3-7?
options: God’s compassion for the lost and desire for their salvation
questions.correctAnswer: God’s compassion for the lost and desire for their salvation
questions.explanation: Luke 15:3-7 reflects the theme of God’s compassion and eagerness to save the lost, just as Jonah 4:11 shows God’s pity for Nineveh’s inhabitants.

theological.title: Jonah Chapter 4 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Jonah Chapter 4 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What was Jonah's emotional response to God's mercy on Nineveh?
questions.correctAnswer: He was very angry
questions.explanation: Jonah was displeased and exceedingly angry because God spared Nineveh. This is stated in Jonah 4:1.

questions.question: Why did Jonah initially flee to Tarshish instead of obeying God's command?
options: He wanted to see the world
He was afraid of the people
He knew God was gracious and merciful
questions.correctAnswer: He knew God was gracious and merciful
questions.explanation: Jonah fled because he knew that God was gracious and merciful, and feared that God would forgive Nineveh, as indicated in Jonah 4:2.

questions.question: What did Jonah ask God to do in his anger?
questions.correctAnswer: To take his life
questions.explanation: In his anger, Jonah wished for God to take his life, believing it was better for him to die than live. This is found in Jonah 4:3.

questions.question: What question did the Lord ask Jonah regarding his anger?
options: Doest thou well to be angry?
questions.correctAnswer: Doest thou well to be angry?
questions.explanation: The Lord asked Jonah if it was right for him to be angry, as stated in Jonah 4:4.

questions.question: What did Jonah do after leaving the city?
questions.correctAnswer: He built a booth
questions.explanation: Jonah went out of the city and built a booth to see what would become of Nineveh, as mentioned in Jonah 4:5.

questions.question: What did God prepare to give Jonah shade?
questions.correctAnswer: A gourd
questions.explanation: God prepared a gourd to provide shade for Jonah, making him glad, as found in Jonah 4:6.

questions.question: What happened to the gourd the next day?
questions.correctAnswer: It withered
questions.explanation: God prepared a worm that caused the gourd to wither, as stated in Jonah 4:7.

questions.question: What did God prepare in addition to the worm?
questions.correctAnswer: A vehement east wind
questions.explanation: God prepared a vehement east wind that caused Jonah to faint from the heat, as noted in Jonah 4:8.

questions.question: How did Jonah respond to the loss of the gourd?
questions.correctAnswer: He wished to die
questions.explanation: Jonah wished to die again, claiming it was better for him to die than to live after the gourd withered, according to Jonah 4:8.

questions.question: What did God say to Jonah regarding his pity for the gourd?
options: You have had pity on the gourd
questions.correctAnswer: You have had pity on the gourd
questions.explanation: God pointed out that Jonah had pity on the gourd, which he did not labor for, in Jonah 4:10.

questions.question: What reason does God give for wanting to spare Nineveh?
options: They cannot discern their right hand from their left
questions.correctAnswer: All of the above
questions.explanation: God expressed the importance of sparing Nineveh, noting their ignorance and the presence of many people and cattle, as stated in Jonah 4:11.

questions.question: What does Jonah 4 reveal about God's character?
options: He is only concerned with Israel
questions.correctAnswer: He is gracious and merciful
questions.explanation: The chapter reveals God's gracious and merciful nature, especially in His willingness to forgive Nineveh, as acknowledged by Jonah in Jonah 4:2.

questions.question: How does Jonah's attitude reflect humanity's struggle with God's mercy?
options: It shows anger towards God's grace
questions.correctAnswer: It shows anger towards God's grace
questions.explanation: Jonah's anger at God's mercy towards Nineveh illustrates humanity's struggle to accept divine grace for others, as seen in Jonah 4:1-2.

questions.question: What combined teaching do verses 10 and 11 convey about God's compassion?
options: God is only concerned with Israel
God does not care about cities
questions.correctAnswer: God values creation
questions.explanation: Verses 10 and 11 together illustrate that God values all of His creation, including the people and animals of Nineveh, showing His compassion beyond Israel.

questions.question: What does the interaction between God and Jonah reveal about the nature of divine authority?
options: Jonah's authority is equal to God's
questions.correctAnswer: God's authority is absolute
questions.explanation: The dialogue shows that God's decisions are final and rooted in His nature, highlighting the absolute authority of God over human emotions and understanding, as seen in Jonah 4:4.
